sequences.invariant_hypothesis: I4: Security-distinct upstream principals from different auth methods (userpass vs jwt) must not collapse into the same downstream entity solely due to matching identifier strings.

sequences.description: Audience mismatch: a JWT minted for aud=vault-app should not be accepted by a role bound to aud=other-app; verify that mismatch is rejected and does not grant secret read.
sequences.invariant_hypothesis: I5: Effective permissions must be bound to the upstream intent expressed by aud; a token with aud not in bound_audiences must not authenticate into a role that grants permissions.

params.description: jwt auth for I5 audience mismatch tests

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control token bound to correct audience could not read allowed secret; setup invalid or policy binding broken
Role accepted JWT with aud not in bound_audiences, granting permissions beyond upstream intent (audience binding bypass)

sequences.description: Numeric bound_claims type coercion: role requires department_id=100; attacker sends department_id=100.7 and attempts to authenticate and read a secret.
sequences.invariant_hypothesis: I5: Claim constraints must be enforced without unsafe numeric coercion; a float value near an integer must not satisfy an integer bound_claim and thereby gain permissions.

params.description: jwt auth for I5 numeric coercion tests

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control token with department_id=100 could not read dept secret; setup invalid or policy binding broken
JWT with department_id=100.7 was accepted for role requiring department_id=100, indicating unsafe numeric coercion and potential over-authorization

sequences.description: Config change + re-auth: user logs in under a permissive role and can read secret; admin tightens role claim constraint; same JWT should be rejected on new login and must not regain access.
sequences.invariant_hypothesis: I5: Effective permissions must reflect current broker policy; after tightening role constraints, re-auth with a JWT that no longer satisfies constraints must not yield a token that can access protected resources.

params.description: jwt auth for I5 role-tighten tests

oracle_checks.violation_description: Baseline failed: user could not read tighten/flag before role was tightened; setup invalid
After tightening role constraints, the same JWT (tier=free) was still accepted, granting permissions beyond current broker policy

sequences.description: Attack: role uses claim_constraints {'sub':'*'} with glob matching. Hypothesis: wildcard constraint unintentionally allows any principal to obtain privileged policy, violating authorization binding intent.
sequences.invariant_hypothesis: I5: A role intended to restrict principals must not become effectively 'allow all' due to glob wildcard constraints; privileged access should not be granted to arbitrary subs.

params.description: jwt mount for I5 glob wildcard tests

oracle_checks.violation_description: Arbitrary principal obtained privileged read via glob wildcard constraint; indicates authorization binding failure due to overly-broad constraint semantics.
Control principal could not read despite role/policy setup; test setup may be broken rather than indicating a security property.

sequences.description: Attack: groups claim maps to an external identity group with privileged policy. Hypothesis: group-derived policies may be applied even when role intent is minimal, causing over-grant.
sequences.invariant_hypothesis: I5: Effective permissions from group claim mapping must not exceed the intersection of upstream intent (groups claim) and broker policy; a user without the privileged group should not gain privileged access, and a user with the group should not gain policies beyond what broker policy intends for that role.

params.description: jwt mount for I5 group escalation tests

oracle_checks.violation_description: User without 'admins' group accessed admin secret; indicates group-policy binding or claim evaluation is bypassed.
User gained admin secret access via groups claim even though role intent is minimal; indicates group-derived policies can exceed BrokerPolicy(config) for the role.

sequences.description: Default-role confusion: mount-level default_role points to privileged role; attacker omits role in login_with_jwt and may receive elevated policy beyond intended minimal role.
sequences.invariant_hypothesis: I5: Effective permissions from a JWT login that omits role must not exceed BrokerPolicy; default_role must not silently grant privileged policies when caller intent is minimal/unspecified.

params.description: jwt mount for I5 default_role tests

oracle_checks.violation_description: JWT login without explicit role was accepted and allowed admin secret read via mount default_role, exceeding intended least-privilege BrokerPolicy.
Control least-priv role should authenticate successfully but must not read admin secret; if it can, policy binding is broken.

sequences.description: Identity policy persistence: user first logs in with privileged role, then role is downgraded and user re-authenticates with least-priv role; check whether prior identity-derived policies persist and still allow admin secret reads.
sequences.invariant_hypothesis: I5: Effective permissions for a new session must be bounded by the current role's granted policies; prior sessions or identity state must not cause policy carry-over after downgrade.

params.description: jwt mount for I5 policy persistence tests

oracle_checks.violation_description: Baseline privileged login should be able to read admin secret; if not, setup is broken and cannot test persistence.
After re-auth with least-role, session still read admin secret, indicating policy carry-over beyond current role intent.
Least-role session should retain ability to read public secret; if denied, test may be misconfigured.
